evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Rep says 'This will just take about seven to ten minutes. Is that okay with you Heather?' but does not frame the full quid pro quo (availability + 10-15 minute timeframe + promise of dependable quote). The opening 'Great, it looks like we have availability' framing and dependable quote promise are absent.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Never asked. Rep jumps straight into logistics probing after confirming the date: 'So to confirm, you are moving from a second floor one bedroom apartment...'
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: N/A — customer did not raise concerns; she raised logistical details about partial move (beds, couch, AC unit, boxes) which rep acknowledged but did not probe deeper. No concerns about the move itself were raised by customer.
evidence_quotes.active_listening_reflection: N/A — no concerns were raised that would require reflection.
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Full. Rep states: 'a typical one bedroom apartment usually takes 2 movers one truck between two and a half to three and a half hours to completely move. So in your case since you are partially moving from our second floor one bedroom apartment to a one story house then I would estimate your move to be...just the minimum two and a half hours. So for two and a half hours. Alright that's gonna be $515.' This anchors to typical range and personalizes to partial move.
evidence_quotes.pricing_framing: Full. Rep discloses: 'no hidden fees of any type no credit card fees, no upfront pay, no deposit, no transportation fees, no disassemble, reassembly fees' and explains minimum/increments: 'we have a two and a half hour minimum and once we go over that the time is prorated in fifteen minute increments.'
evidence_quotes.feels_fair_then_silence: Not asked. Rep moves directly from estimate ($515) to explicit ask ('So would you like our help with your upcoming move today?') with no 'does that feel fair' or equivalent, and no pause for customer reflection.
evidence_quotes.on_time_guarantee_delivered: Full. Rep states: 'if we can't make it in the time window that we arrange, we immediately start discounting money of your final bill.'
evidence_quotes.damage_coverage_delivered: Full. Rep states: 'our free evaluation coverage included in our hourly rate provides up to $2,000 per move to repair, replace or reimburse for accidental damages. So unlike others will charge you extra for it or offer only state mandated 60¢ per pound coverage.'
evidence_quotes.closes_the_loop: No. Rep does not ask 'Does that put those to rest?' or equivalent after delivering the Two Promises.
evidence_quotes.final_concerns_check: Throwaway. Rep asks 'will there be anything else?' — a minimal empty check, not a genuine 'What's still concerning you about this move?'
evidence_quotes.catch_all_asked: No. Rep never asks 'Anything coming with you we haven't talked about?' or equivalent.
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: Full. Rep asks plainly: 'So would you like our help with your upcoming move today?' with no built-in out or soft alternative offered.
evidence_quotes.rate_lock_mentioned: No. Rep does not mention rate lock or that the quote holds/is guaranteed.
evidence_quotes.booking_confirmed: Partial. Rep confirms the date (Friday October 2nd, 8:30-9:00 AM window) and mentions sending email details, but customer explicitly requests to hold and call back. Rep does not confirm phone number, crew size, full addresses, or crew notes about customer's concerns. No actual booking was completed — customer deferred.

top_strength: Rep thoroughly gathered all logistics details needed (property type, floors, rooms, parking, access concerns, special items, box count) and delivered a personalized, anchored estimate with full pricing transparency and both key promises.
coaching_note: Ask 'What are your biggest concerns about this move?' in Section 2 before diving into logistics probing—you jumped straight to details without understanding what the customer actually wanted to solve for on the call.
